intro: In Sivas province stands Şifaiye Madrasa, a madrasa and hospital dating from 1217. It was the hospital and medical school built for Kaykaus I, and his tiled tomb is set in the south iwan of the courtyard. Here, music and running water were part of the treatment.
history: The building was raised in 1217 for the Seljuk sultan Kaykaus I, and it was both hospital and medical school. When the sultan died of tuberculosis, he was buried in the tiled tomb set in the south iwan of the courtyard. Healing here went beyond medicine: running water and music were part of the treatment, and the pool at the centre of the court belonged to that regime. Pause for a moment and imagine the sound of water and music filling this courtyard.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the tomb of Kaykaus and the courtyard pool. Then take in the iwans, and the portal.
facts: Did you know? The tiled inscription on the tomb carries lines the sultan had written about his own death, an unusual choice for a Seljuk ruler. The building was both hospital and medical school, and running water and music were part of the treatment. Sultan Kaykaus I, who died of tuberculosis, was buried in the tiled tomb in the south iwan of the courtyard.
outro: This brings our tour of Şifaiye Madrasa to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This was a place of healing for centuries; let it keep its peace for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
